source_refs.note: Exercise 3.3, Question 23: book p. 89-90, 24 questions (integration by parts); answer key p. 301 (printed under 'Exercise 3.5')

blocks.explanation:
Phir se \(\sqrt{x}\) do jagah hai, aur denominator mein \(\sqrt{x}\) hai, to \(t = \sqrt{x}\) rakhne se \(\frac{dx}{\sqrt{x}} = 2\,dt\) ban jata hai.
Integral \(2\int e^t(1 + t)\,dt\) reh jata hai.
Ab shakal dekhiye: \(e^t[f(t) + f'(t)]\) with \(f(t) = t\), kyunke \(t + 1 = t + \frac{d}{dt}t\). Is liye jawab \(2te^t\)!
Plan: substitution, parts se dikhayein ke integrals cancel hote hain, wapas \(x\).
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\int \frac{e^{\sqrt{x}}(1 + \sqrt{x})}{\sqrt{x}}\,dx\), \(x > 0\).
Maloom karna: indefinite integral.
Tareeqa: \(t = \sqrt{x}\); phir \(2\int e^t(t + 1)\,dt\), aur \(\int te^t\,dt\) parts se.

Substitution
\[t = \sqrt{x} \Rightarrow \dfrac{dx}{\sqrt{x}} = 2\,dt\]
\[= 2\int e^t(1 + t)\,dt\]
Kyun: \(dt = \frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}\,dx\), is liye \(\frac{dx}{\sqrt{x}} = 2\,dt\); \(e^{\sqrt{x}} = e^t\) aur \(1 + \sqrt{x} = 1 + t\).

\(\int te^t\,dt\) par parts
\[\int te^t\,dt = te^t - \int e^t\,dt = te^t - e^t\]
Kyun: \(t\) first aur \(e^t\) second; \(t\) ka derivative 1.

Jor dein
\[2\int e^t(t + 1)\,dt = 2\left(te^t - e^t + e^t\right) + c\]
\[= 2te^t + c = 2\sqrt{x}e^{\sqrt{x}} + c\]
Kyun: \(\int e^t\,dt = e^t\) ne \(-e^t\) ko cancel kar diya; yahi \(e^t[f + f'] \to e^tf\) wala Note hai. Phir \(t = \sqrt{x}\).
Dhyan dein: aakhir mein 2 se zarb aur \(t = \sqrt{x}\) wapas rakhna na bhoolein.

Tasdeeq
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}(2\sqrt{x}e^{\sqrt{x}}) = \dfrac{e^{\sqrt{x}}}{\sqrt{x}} + 2\sqrt{x}e^{\sqrt{x}}\cdot\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}\]
\[= \dfrac{e^{\sqrt{x}}(1 + \sqrt{x})}{\sqrt{x}}\]
Kyun: product aur chain rule; common \(\frac{e^{\sqrt{x}}}{\sqrt{x}}\) lene se integrand mila.
